          Overview

          The interfaces of vaxpunk's executive and the PAL below it, as code written against them sees them. Every entry is read from the sources by scripts/apidoc.py: the comment above each routine and macro, the system service vector, and the tables of DESIGN-0001. How the pieces fit is in DESIGN-0001 (the PAL) and DESIGN-0002 (the executive).

          Press / to search. Every name in the text links to its entry. Status lists the condition values found in a routine's code and in what it calls whose failure it passes on. A Limit is a deliberate shortcut, with the way past it.

          TagHow it is called
          ServiceSYS$name with CALLS or CALLG, or the $name_S macro; CHMK, or for $CMEXEC CHME, takes it to the executive
          CALLCALLS or CALLG: arguments in the argument list at AP, status in R0, RET
          JSBJSB or BSBW: arguments and results in registers, RSB
          Handleran SCB vector: the PAL delivers an interrupt, an exception or CHMx to it; it ends with REI
          PALa privileged VAX instruction, or CALL_PAL; vmacro compiles it into svc #0
          Macroa macro from a .LIBRARY; Definitions macros define symbols

          1System services

          Called from any mode with CALLS or CALLG to SYS$name, which is in syssrv.mar, or with the $name_S macros of starlet.mlb. Programs run in user mode, and SYS$name is in the vector, a page user mode may run. A service called with fewer arguments than it takes returns SS$_INSFARG, and one with an argument list or an address its caller's mode can't reach SS$_ACCVIO.

          $CREPRC

          Serviceroottask/exec/process.mar:172
          Format
          SYS$CREPRC pidadr, image, input, output, error, prvadr, quota, prcnam, baspri, uic, mbxunt, stsflg
          Macro
          $CREPRC_S PIDADR=0, IMAGE=0, INPUT=0, OUTPUT=0, ERROR=0, PRVADR=0, QUOTA=0, PRCNAM=0, BASPRI=#2, UIC=#0, MBXUNT=#0, STSFLG=#0
          Dispatch
          CHMK #0 to EXE$CMODKRNL, which calls EXE$CREPRC with at least 12 arguments
          Description

          Makes a process that runs image, called prcnam, at priority baspri, and puts its PID in pidadr. The other arguments are ignored: there is no I/O, privilege, quota or UIC yet.

          Status
          SS$_NORMAL SS$_ACCVIO SS$_EXQUOTA SS$_DUPLNAM SS$_INSFARG SS$_INSFMEM SS$_IVLOGNAM

          Data
          SCH$GL_CURPCB SCH$GL_PCBVEC SCH$GL_SEQ SGN$GW_QUANTUM

          $DELPRC

          Serviceroottask/exec/process.mar:539
          Format
          SYS$DELPRC pidadr, prcnam
          Macro
          $DELPRC_S PIDADR=0, PRCNAM=0
          Dispatch
          CHMK #1 to EXE$CMODKRNL, which calls EXE$DELPRC with at least 2 arguments
          Description

          Deletes a process, the current one if none is named. Another one's P0 and P1 aren't the current process's, so it runs itself down: it leaves its slot at once, so no one finds it any more, ends any wait, and deletes itself the next time it has the CPU, when SCH$SCHED returns to it or it starts.

          Limit. a flag the scheduler checks, standing in for VMS's kernel AST.

          Status

          2Executive routines

          Routines and data of EXEC.EXE, by module. Programs link against SYS.STB, so kernel-mode code reaches every global here directly. The system services' own routines, EXE$name, are in chapter 1; local routines can only be called from their own module.

          2.1EVENT Event flag services

          roottask/exec/event.mar:1

          Each process has 128 event flags in four clusters of 32. Clusters 0 and 1 (flags 0-63) are its own, local. Clusters 2 and 3 (64-127) are common: $ASCEFC associates each with a common event block, a named cluster that every process associated with it shares, which is how processes synchronize with each other. A process waiting for flags is in the LEF state for local ones and in the CEB's wait queue, state CEF, for common ones; $SETEF wakes those whose wait it satisfies.

          2.2EXEC The executive's start, and the swapper

          roottask/exec/exec.mar:1

          The root task, the PAL, starts EXEC.EXE as a task of its own, in kernel mode at IPL 31, with R11 pointing at the restart parameter block (docs/design/0001-pal-interface.md). EXEC$START sets up the system control block, memory, the scheduler and the system time, starts the STARTUP process and becomes the swapper, process 1, which deletes what deleted processes leave behind (docs/design/0002-executive-processes.md).

          2.3MEMORY Memory management: pages, pool and the memory services

          roottask/exec/memory.mar:1

          The PAL gives the executive physical pages, numbered by PFN, and maps one at an address when the executive writes a PTE with WRPTE. The executive owns the PFN database, here a list of free PFNs, and decides what goes where (docs/design/0002-executive-processes.md). P0 and P1 are each process's own; a PTE written there is the current process's:

            ^X00010000  P0: the process's image, then its $EXPREG pages
  ^X40010000  S0, every process's: EXEC.EXE
  ^X48000000  nonpaged pool: PCBs, kernel stacks, common event blocks
  ^X4FFF0000  the RPB; ^X50000000 the boot volume, read-only
  ^X5FFF0000  the boot stack's top
  ^X60000000  P1: the process's $CRETVA pages, its mode stacks at the top

          The PFN database and the pool are synchronized at IPL$_SYNCH.

          2.4PROCESS Process creation, deletion and control

          roottask/exec/process.mar:1

          A process is a PCB and a kernel stack in S0, an image and stacks in its own P0 and P1, and the threads the PAL makes for it: the first time the scheduler switches to the process's HWPCB, and the first time it enters each outer mode. $CREPRC builds the PCB and a kernel stack holding the frame REI pops, which starts the process at EXE$PROCSTRT, in kernel mode at IPL 0. There it activates its image from the boot volume and REIs to user mode, which calls the image; when the image returns, or calls $EXIT, the process is deleted, as a VMS process is when its image exits and it has no command interpreter (docs/design/0002-executive-processes.md).

          2.5QIO Channels and I/O to the console

          roottask/exec/qio.mar:1

          A process writes on the console as on VMS: $ASSIGN gives it a channel to OPA0:, and $QIO or $QIOW writes a buffer on it. The write is done before $QIO returns, which then sets the event flag and the I/O status block, so $QIOW is $QIO (docs/design/0002-executive-processes.md).

          Limit. the console is the only device, written a buffer at a time at IPL$_SYNCH, so lines don't mix; a terminal driver with I/O request packets replaces this.

          2.6SCHED The scheduler

          roottask/exec/sched.mar:1

          Processes are threads in the executive's address space, and only one of them runs at a time: the current process, SCH$GL_CURPCB. The others wait in a state queue: one per priority for those that are computable (COM), one per wait state for the rest (docs/design/0002-executive-processes.md). The scheduler's database is synchronized at IPL$_SYNCH, as on a uniprocessor VMS: below it, the reschedule interrupt at IPL$_RESCHED may take the CPU away; at or above it, nothing does.

          A process gives up the CPU by calling SCH$SCHED, which picks the highest computable process and hands it the CPU with SWPCTX. The PAL keeps each process's registers in its own thread, so the switch saves nothing: the process leaving waits inside its SWPCTX until the CPU comes back to it.

          The interval timer takes the CPU from a process whose quantum is up, if another computable one has its priority or a higher one: SCH$QEND, round robin within a priority.

          2.7SYSSRV The system service vector, the change mode dispatchers

          roottask/exec/syssrv.mar:1

          A program calls a system service as on VMS, with CALLS or CALLG to SYS$name, or with the $name_S macros in starlet.mlb. SYS$name changes mode to kernel with CHMK and the service's code; the PAL delivers the CHMK through the SCB to EXE$CMODKRNL, which checks the argument list and calls the service's EXE$name routine with it, then REIs with its status in R0. $CMEXEC changes mode to executive instead, with CHME, which EXE$CMODEXEC serves.

          Programs run in user mode, so SYS$name, EXE$CMODEXEC and EXE$USRSTART, where a process enters user mode, are in a page of their own, the vector, which EXEC$START makes user readable: code an outer mode may run, as VMS's system service vector is.

          Services that aren't implemented yet are stubs that return SS$_ILLSER. An access violation or a reserved instruction in an outer mode ends the process.

          EXE$VECTOR

          2.8TIMESCHDL The interval timer, the system time and the timer queue

          roottask/exec/timeschdl.mar:1

          The PAL delivers the interval timer interrupt every 10 ms, at IPL$_HWCLK, wherever the current process is (docs/adr/0004-interval-timer-is-a-pal-thread.md). As on VMS, the hardware clock's handler does as little as it can: it advances the system time, charges the tick to the current process's quantum and, when the quantum is up or the first timer queue entry is due, requests the software timer interrupt, whose handler does the rest at a lower IPL (docs/design/0002-executive-processes.md).

          Times are VMS's: a quadword of 100 ns units since 17-Nov-1858 00:00, or, negative, a delta from now. The timer queue holds what $SETIMR and $SCHDWK asked for, in the order it is due. It is synchronized at IPL$_SYNCH; the system time, and EXE$GQ_1ST_TIME, which the hardware clock's handler reads, at IPL$_HWCLK.

          EXE$INITTIM

          JSBroottask/exec/timeschdl.mar:49
          Linkage
          JSB G^EXE$INITTIM; arguments in registers, returns with RSB
          Description

          Makes the timer queue empty and sets the system time from the RTC's, which the PAL put in the RPB. IPL 31.

          Limit. EMUL is signed, so the RTC's seconds work until 2038.

          Registers
          Uses R0-R2.
          Called by
          EXEC$START
          Data
          EXE$GL_RPB EXE$GQ_SYSTIME EXE$GQ_TQFL

          EXE$HWCLKINT

          Handlerroottask/exec/timeschdl.mar:67
          Linkage
          reached through the SCB; returns with REI
          Description

          The interval timer interrupt, at IPL$_HWCLK. Advances the system time, and requests the software timer interrupt if the first timer queue entry is due, or if the current process's quantum is up: it counts up from -SGN$GW_QUANTUM to 0. A tick before SCH$INIT, or while the CPU is idle in SCH$SCHED, has no process to charge.

          2.9CONSOLIO Console output, as VMS's EXE$OUT* routines

          vtools/lib/consolio.mar:1

          The routines VMS's own bugcheck and init code print on the console with, and drivers too: called with JSB, arguments in registers. Like VMS's, they take no lock and don't change IPL; callers who share the console take it first. R11 selects the device on the VAX, 0 for the console; it is ignored, as on Alpha. Link this module with the program: vmacro compiles it. CON$PUTCHAR, the one part that knows the hardware, comes from elsewhere: conputchar.mar under vrun, the executive's own under the PAL.

          EXE$READEF EXE$CRETVA EXE$DELTVA EXE$EXPREG EXE$NAMPID EXE$CREPRC EXE$SETPRI EXE$ASSIGN EXE$QIO EXE$GETTIM

          REI

          PALDESIGN-0001
          Format
          CALL_PAL #^X92
          VAX
          REI
          Code
          ^X92, any mode; Alpha
          In
          —
          Out
          —
          Description

          Pops a frame: PC, PSL, registers, SPs

          Used by

          3.2Calling the PAL

          From DESIGN-0001, Calling the PAL.

          The executive calls the PAL with svc #0:

          RegisterInOut
          x7function codeunchanged
          x0a0, the first argumentv0, the result, if the call has one
          x1-x5a1-a5unchanged
          x6, x8-x30, sp, NZCVnot seen by the PALunchanged

          3.3VAX instructions that are PAL calls

          From DESIGN-0001, How MACRO-32 calls it.

          VAX instructionPAL call
          MTPR src, #PR$_IPLMTPR_IPL, a0 = src
          MFPR #PR$_IPL, dstMFPR_IPL, dst = v0
          MFPR #PR$_PCBB, dstMFPR_PCBB
          MTPR src, #PR$_SCBB, MFPR #PR$_SCBB, dstMTPR_SCBB, MFPR_SCBB
          MTPR src, #PR$_SIRRMTPR_SIRR
          MFPR #PR$_SISR, dstMFPR_SISR
          MTPR src, #PR$_TXDBMTPR_TXDB
          CHMK #code, CHME, CHMS, CHMUCHMK, CHME, CHMS, CHMU, R0 = code; R0 isn't kept
          PROBER mode, len, base, PROBEWPROBER, PROBEW, a0 = base, a1 = len, a2 = mode; Z set if v0 is 0, no access
          REIREI
          HALTHALT
          CALL_PAL #codeany call: a0-a5 in R0-R5, v0 in R0, as on Alpha

          3.4What the PAL sets up

          From DESIGN-0001, What the PAL sets up.

          system space every process shares (Memory):

          AddressWhatProtection
          0x40010000 upEXEC.EXE's sections, at their link addressestheirs
          0x4FFF0000the restart parameter block, one pagekernel write
          0x50000000 upthe boot volumekernel read
          0x5FFEC000-0x5FFF0000the boot stack, 16 KBkernel write

          3.5The restart parameter block

          From DESIGN-0001, The restart parameter block.

          $RPBDEF in vtools/lib/lib.mlb, longwords:

          OffsetFieldHolds
          0RPB$L_BASEthe RPB's address
          4RPB$L_PFNCNThow many PFNs the executive has: 0 to PFNCNT - 1
          8RPB$L_FREEPFNthe PFNs below this one hold what the PAL set up
          12RPB$L_VOLUMEthe boot volume's address
          16RPB$L_VOLSIZEits size in bytes
          20RPB$L_BOOTTIMEseconds since 1970 at boot, from QEMU virt's PL031 RTC, which the PAL maps after the UART and reads once
          64RPB$Q_HWPCBthe boot context's HWPCB, 128 bytes

          3.6Page table entries

          From DESIGN-0001, Memory.

          sign-extended longwords reach (ADR-0005):

          RegionAddressesWhose
          P00x00000000-0x3FFFFFFFthe current process's: its image, from 0x10000
          S00x40000000-0x5FFFFFFFthe system's, the same in every process
          P10x60000000-0x7FFFFFFFthe current process's: its stacks, at the top

          A PTE is the VAX's longword ($PTEDEF), with one change:

          BitsFieldMeaning
          31Vvalid: the page is mapped
          30:27PROTthe VAX protection code ($PRTDEF): who may read and write
          25EXECnew: instructions may run from the page; ARM64 has the permission, the VAX had none
          20:0PFNthe page frame

          3.7The interrupt frame

          From DESIGN-0001, Interrupts and exceptions.

          OffsetHolds
          0PC
          8PSL
          16R7
          24the interrupted VAX SP
          32the interrupted ARM64 sp
          40-80x13-x18, vmacro's scratch registers
          88x30

          3.8Faults and HALT

          From DESIGN-0001, Faults and HALT.

          took it:

          EventThe PAL prints
          Page fault%PAL-F-ACCVIO with the address and PC
          Undefined instruction, brk (BPT)%PAL-F-OPCDEC with the PC
          Reserved PAL call, bad WRPTE%PAL-F-OPCDEC with the code, PC, R0 and R1
          Delivery with no vector or stack%PAL-F-NOVEC
          REI without a frame%PAL-F-REI
          HALT%PAL-I-HALT with the PC and R0

          3.9The Alpha OpenVMS calls

          From DESIGN-0001, The Alpha calls.

          Privileged, 0x00-0x3F:

          CodeCallsvaxpunk
          0x00HALTkept, implemented
          0x01, 0x02DRAINA, CFLUSHdropped: seL4 does cache maintenance on frames
          0x03, 0x04LDQP, STQPdropped: the executive has no physical addresses
          0x05SWPCTXchanged, implemented: contexts are threads, made on first switch, deleted by DELCTX
          0x06MFPR_ASNdropped: address space numbers are seL4's
          0x07, 0x08, 0x26, 0x27MTPR_ASTEN, MTPR_ASTSR, MFPR_ASTEN, MFPR_ASTSRkept
          0x09, 0x0ACSERVE, SWPPALdropped: firmware services
          0x0B, 0x0CMFPR_FEN, MTPR_FENkept, with floating point
          0x0DMTPR_IPIRkept, with more than one CPU
          0x0E, 0x0FMFPR_IPL, MTPR_IPLkept, implemented
          0x10, 0x11MFPR_MCES, MTPR_MCESkept
          0x12MFPR_PCBBkept, implemented
          0x13, 0x14MFPR_PRBR, MTPR_PRBRkept
          0x15MFPR_PTBRdropped: page tables are the PAL's
          0x16, 0x17MFPR_SCBB, MTPR_SCBBkept, implemented
          0x18, 0x19MTPR_SIRR, MFPR_SISRkept, implemented
          0x1A-0x1D, 0x24, 0x25MFPR_TBCHK, MTPR_TBIA, MTPR_TBIAP, MTPR_TBIS, MTPR_TBISD, MTPR_TBISIchanged: WRPTE
          0x1E-0x23MFPR_ESP, MTPR_ESP, MFPR_SSP, MTPR_SSP, MFPR_USP, MTPR_USPkept
          0x29, 0x2AMFPR_VPTB, MTPR_VPTBdropped: no virtual page table
          0x2B, 0x2EMTPR_PERFMON, MTPR_DATFXdropped
          0x30-0x33MFPR_VIRBND, MTPR_VIRBND, MFPR_SYSPTBR, MTPR_SYSPTBRdropped: page tables are the PAL's
          0x3EWTINTkept, implemented: the idle loop waits for an interrupt
          0x3FMFPR_WHAMIkept

          Unprivileged, 0x80-0xBF:

          CodeCallsvaxpunk
          0x80BPTkept; today BPT is brk, an undefined-instruction fault
          0x81BUGCHKkept
          0x82-0x85CHME, CHMK, CHMS, CHMUchanged, implemented: the PAL moves the call to the process's thread for that mode
          0x86IMBkept
          0x87-0x8E, 0x93-0x9A, 0xA2-0xA9INSQHIL ... REMQUEQ/D, the resident formskept; INSQUE and REMQUE are inline code, since one thread runs at a time
          0x8F, 0x90PROBER, PROBEWkept, implemented
          0x91, 0x92RD_PS, REIkept; REI implemented
          0x9B, 0x9CSWASTEN, WR_PS_SWkept
          0x9DRSCCkept
          0x9E, 0x9FREAD_UNQ, WRITE_UNQdropped: user mode writes TPIDR_EL0 itself
          0xA0, 0xA1AMOVRR, AMOVRMdropped: ARM64 has atomics
          0xAAGENTRAPkept
          0xAECLRFENkept, with floating point

          vaxpunk's own, 0x40-0x7F:

          CodeCallStands in for
          0x40MTPR_TXDBthe VAX console transmit register
          0x41WRPTEwriting a PTE in memory, then MTPR_TBIS
          0x42DELCTXthe PAL's half of deleting a process

Each mode's stack pointer is where the PAL pushes a frame on entering it from an outer mode, and where it saves the stack pointer of a mode it leaves for another.

          4.3starlet.mlb

          starlet.mlb: what programs that call system services use, like VMS's STARLET.MLB. Use it with .LIBRARY "starlet.mlb" and vasm -I vtools/lib.

          4.4vrun.mlb

          vtools/lib/vrun.mlb:1

          vrun.mlb: macros for programs that run under vrun, one per monitor call (docs/runner-abi.md). Use it with .LIBRARY "vrun.mlb" and vasm -I vtools/lib. A vaxpunk macro library is a text file of .MACRO definitions. vmacro (MACRO-32) can use it too, so expressions avoid << and >>.

          $EXIT

          Macrovtools/lib/vrun.mlb:8
          Format
          $EXIT STATUS=1
          Description

          Ends the run. STATUS is a VMS condition value; the default is SS$_NORMAL.

          Expansion
          show
                  movz    x0, #((STATUS) & ^XFFFF)
        movk    x0, #(((STATUS) / 65536) & ^XFFFF), lsl #16
        svc     #1

          $PUT

          Macrovtools/lib/vrun.mlb:16
          Format
          $PUT TEXT, ?STRING, ?AFTER
          Description

          Writes TEXT to the console. TEXT is written as for .ASCII, for example "Hello"<10>; it goes into $LITERAL$. Uses x0 and x1.

          Expansion
          show
                  .SAVE_PSECT
        .PSECT  $LITERAL$
STRING: .ASCII  TEXT
AFTER:
        .RESTORE_PSECT
        adr     x0, STRING
        mov     x1, #AFTER - STRING
        svc     #2

          $WRITE

          Macrovtools/lib/vrun.mlb:29
          Format
          $WRITE ADDRESS, LENGTH
          Description

          Writes LENGTH bytes from ADDRESS, both registers. Uses x0 and x1, so LENGTH can't be x0.

          Expansion
          show
                  mov     x0, ADDRESS
        mov     x1, LENGTH
        svc     #2

          $DUMP

          Macrovtools/lib/vrun.mlb:36
          Format
          $DUMP
          Description

          Prints every register.

          Expansion
          show
                  svc     #3

          4.5sysexe.mlb

          roottask/sysexe/sysexe.mlb:1

          sysexe.mlb: console output for the boot volume's programs, which run in user mode and print with PUT_LINE in lib/print.mar, a line on OPA0: with $QIOW. Each line is written whole, so no other process's comes in between.

          PRINT

          Macroroottask/sysexe/sysexe.mlb:7
          Format
          PRINT TEXT, ?L
          Description

          Writes text and CR LF. Uses R0-R1.

          Expansion
          show
                  .EXTERNAL PUT_LINE
        .SAVE_PSECT LOCAL_BLOCK
        .PSECT  $LITERAL$
L:      .ASCIC  TEXT
        .RESTORE_PSECT
        PUSHAB  L
        CALLS   #1, G^PUT_LINE

          PRINTHEX

          Macroroottask/sysexe/sysexe.mlb:18
          Format
          PRINTHEX TEXT, VALUE, ?L
          Description

          Writes text, value in hex, and CR LF. Uses R0-R1.

          Expansion
          show
                  .EXTERNAL PUT_LINE
        .SAVE_PSECT LOCAL_BLOCK
        .PSECT  $LITERAL$
L:      .ASCIC  TEXT
        .RESTORE_PSECT
        PUSHL   VALUE
        PUSHAB  L
        CALLS   #2, G^PUT_LINE

          EXPECT

          Macroroottask/sysexe/sysexe.mlb:31
          Format
          EXPECT STATUS, N, ?OK
          Description

          Returns 2 * n, an error the executive reports with the process's name, unless R0 is status.

          Expansion
          show
                  CMPL    R0, STATUS
        BEQL    OK
        MOVL    #<N * 2>, R0
        RET
OK:
